content: Crop rotation should be followed to break the life cycle of pink bollworm. Use authentic Bt-cotton seeds and follow timely sowing practices. Avoid excessive nitrogenous fertilizer and monitor fields using pheromone traps from 45 DAS.
Economic threshold level for pink bollworm is 10 percent damaged flowers or green bolls. Threshold is also considered crossed when pheromone traps catch 8 moths continuously for 3 days.

Monitor whitefly on alternate hosts and weeds before sowing. Maintain field sanitation and avoid excessive urea application. Install yellow sticky traps during July and August. Neem oil sprays are useful during the initial crop stage.
Recommended insecticides for whitefly include Diafenthiuron, Dinotefuran, Flonicamid, Pyriproxyfen, Spiromesifen, Clothianidin and Afidopyropen.
Recommended sprays for jassid management include Flonicamid, Dinotefuran, Imidacloprid, Tolfenpyrad and Fenpyroximate.
Thrips can be managed using Thiamethoxam, Spinetoram or Profenofos sprays based on infestation severity.
For mixed infestation of whitefly and thrips, Diafenthiuron, Spinetoram or Profenofos may be used. For mixed infestation of whitefly and jassid, Flonicamid or Dinotefuran are recommended.
Keep fields and bunds weed free especially from Parthenium weed. Install blue sticky traps and manage thrips infestation to reduce tobacco streak virus transmission.
Recommended insecticides for bollworms include Chlorantraniliprole, Flubendiamide, Indoxacarb and Spinosad depending on crop stage and infestation.
Economic threshold level for mealybugs is when more than 20 plants per acre show grade II, III or IV damage symptoms.
Recommended insecticides after 120 DAS include Cypermethrin, Lambda cyhalothrin, Deltamethrin, Fenpropathrin and Alphacypermethrin.
Terminate the crop early when economically feasible. Avoid extending cotton crop beyond 180 days. Remove stalks and allow grazing after picking to reduce bollworm carryover.

Seed treatment with Carboxin plus Thiram, Pseudomonas fluorescens, Fluxapyroxad or Tetraconazole is recommended for root rot management. Drenching with Trichoderma or Carbendazim may help symptomatic plants.
Use resistant Bt hybrids and maintain weed sanitation. Border crops like sorghum and maize help reduce disease spread. Whitefly management is critical for controlling CLCuD.
Follow crop rotation, deep ploughing and proper drainage. Avoid water stagnation. Drenching with Copper oxychloride or Carbendazim along with Urea may help reduce parawilt symptoms.
Foliar sprays of Copper oxychloride, Carbendazim plus Mancozeb or Copper sulphate plus Mancozeb are recommended at weekly intervals.
Preventive sprays of Propineb, Azoxystrobin plus Difenoconazole, Fluxapyroxad plus Pyraclostrobin or Propiconazole are recommended.
Boll rot can be managed using Fluxapyroxad plus Pyraclostrobin, Metiram plus Pyraclostrobin or Propineb sprays during boll maturity stage.

Remove dried petals sticking to developing bolls. Avoid excessive nitrogenous fertilizers and ensure proper field drainage. Copper oxychloride or Carbendazim plus Mancozeb sprays may help under humid conditions.
Grey mildew can be managed using Kresoxim-methyl or Azoxystrobin plus Difenoconazole sprays.
Rust disease can be managed using Fluxapyroxad plus Pyraclostrobin, Metiram plus Pyraclostrobin, Propiconazole or Azoxystrobin plus Difenoconazole sprays.
